title: Agents publish to refs/agents/<agent>, never a remote branch
goal: CEO decision 2026-11-11: move agent inbox branches off GitHub branches so no agent push creates a pull-request surface. push-policy admits refs/agents/<agent> (create, fast-forward, deletion at its tip) and refuses creating or updating refs/heads/local-agent/<agent> with a message naming refs/agents/<agent>, while deleting one stays allowed (retirement, building on T-RETIREBR-1). IntegrationPolicy publishes to refs/agents/<agent> (publish_ref) and refuses local-agent targets (RetiredAgentBranch); the git governor fetches +refs/agents/*:refs/remotes/<remote>-agents/* (pruned) and sweeps each agent ref as local-agent/<agent>, still reading legacy remote local-agent branches read-only. docs/agent-refs.md documents layout, publishing, inspection, adoption and the transition.
host: CEO laptop, CachyOS Linux x86_64, 28 threads; other agents building (cargo -j 8, nice 19)

results.xtask: cargo test --offline --locked --no-fail-fast -p xtask: 29 binaries, 613 passed, 1 failed (ci_workflow_perf::no_gate_or_hook_depends_on_the_retired_target_guard, already failing on origin/main since 192b53d27; reads scripts/parallel-workflow.sh, untouched here); native_push_policy 16/16, 3 new tests fail on the previous push_policy.rs
results.susi_harness: cargo test --offline --locked --no-fail-fast -p susi-harness: 11 binaries, 575 passed, 0 failed
results.guards: cargo test -p susi --test architecture_tests --test orphan_sources --test lean_core_ceilings --test core_docs_promise_no_ui_or_plugins --test no_github_coupling: all pass; susi-harness src measures exactly its 37,439-line ceiling (new code compressed to fit, ceiling unchanged)

limitations: core local-workflow has no `ship --adopt` and reads no remote agent branch; it gates the claimed worktree it is given, so it needed no change. Adoption of a remote agent ref is a fetch into the origin-agents mirror and a merge into a claimed worktree, or susi-harness integrate/submit-main (docs/agent-refs.md).
The sweep's fetch now uses --prune, so remote-tracking refs of branches deleted on the remote disappear from refs/remotes/<remote>/ as well as the agent mirror.
push-policy is a client-side hook; a push with --no-verify or from a clone without core.hooksPath is not checked. Host-side rules are a CEO decision.
docs/harness-coordination.md (a design note, not in this claim) still describes pushing refs/heads/local-agent/<agent>.
